validated_incidents.title: Phoenix, Arizona ball of flame sighting
validated_incidents.summary: A seven-inch ball of flame with an eight-foot trail was sighted from Phoenix, Arizona on July 2, 1952, at 0420 hours, traveling in an arc from northwest to southwest over approximately 3-4 minutes.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: (1) SEVEN INCH BALL OF FLAME WITH EIGHT FOOT TRAIL SIGHTED. NO SOUND OR LIGHTS RESEMBLING KNOWN FLYING OBJECTS. (2) SIGHTED AT @42@ ON 2 JULY 1952 FoR 3 TO 4 MINUTES.
validated_incidents.reporting_unit: 427TH PLT TNG WG LUKE AFB ARIZ
validated_incidents.size_description: seven inch ball with eight foot trail
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: No known aircraft or balloons reported; possibility of crop dusters mentioned; search requested

validated_incidents.title: Tremonton, Utah UFO Filming
validated_incidents.summary: Chief Petty Officer Delbert C. Newhouse filmed approximately 30 feet of 16mm color motion picture film showing a group of 10-12 unidentified objects milling about in rough formation proceeding westerly near Tremonton, Utah. One object reversed course and was tracked separately across the camera field of view multiple times.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: Movies were taken seven miles north of Tremonton, Utah, on U.S. Highway 30S at 1110 MST on 2 July 52, Gamera used was a Bell and Howell Auto Mester with the three inch telephoto lens, Gamera was hand-held. First few feet of film were taken at FeS; balance at F416, Sixteen fPalies per Second were used, Movies were taken by Chief Petty Officer Delbert C. Newhouse, 177273 Aviation Supply Depot, Naval Supply Center, Oaklend, Calif, Newhouse wes driving from Washington, D,C., to Portland, Oregon, on the morning of 2 July 52 when his wife noticed a group of objects in the sky that she could not identify.
validated_incidents.location_text: seven miles north of Tremonton, Utah, on U.S. Highway 30S
validated_incidents.reporting_unit: Aviation Supply Depot, Naval Supply Center, Oakland, California
validated_incidents.shape_description: gun metal colored objects shaped like two saucers, one inverted on top of the other; oblate or disk shaped
validated_incidents.size_description: subtended about the same angle as B-29s at 10,000 feet (about half a degree); maximum and minimum size 98 and 16 feet
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Analysis ruled out balloons, birds, aircraft based on acceleration and velocity computations; hypothesis of light sources or highly reflective non-spherical objects; some analysis suggested seagulls or pillow balloons but evidence was contradictory

validated_incidents.title: Lubbock, Texas sightings and photographs
validated_incidents.summary: Five Texas Tech college professors observed multiple formations of lights passing over Lubbock on multiple nights in late August 1951, with measurements indicating angular velocity of 30 degrees per second. A student photographer captured images of the formations.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: These five college professors from Texas Tech were sitting out in the backyard one evening, in what was it, August, yes, August 25th, and they happened to be discussing meteors and so they were sitting there looking up in the sky, and all of a sudden this bunch of lights went over.
validated_incidents.occurred_at_text: August 25, 1951 and subsequent nights through August 31
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Possibly ducks reflecting city lights, though professors rejected this explanation; could be hoax, but photographic evidence examined under microscope showed actual images with varying positions across frames

validated_incidents.title: Lubbock top-shaped object sighting
validated_incidents.summary: Two women driving along the Texas plains observed a top-shaped, silver object hovering over the prairie that accelerated when they approached it.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: two women were driving along in a car, and all of a sudden they looked out over the Texas plains and they saw this object that they described as being top-shaped, like one of these old-fashioned tops you put a string around and pull, and it was silver and it was hovering along over the prairie.
validated_incidents.occurred_at_text: within two or three days of August 31, 1951

validated_incidents.title: Sandia base guard sighting
validated_incidents.summary: A guard and his wife at Sandia base in Albuquerque observed a large dark shape resembling a flying wing aircraft hovering approximately 150 feet overhead with visible exhaust flames.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: a guard and his wife from the Sandia base in Albuquerque were sitting out in their backyard, and all of a sudden they looked up and they saw this big dark shape go over. And they said that it was, it looked a lot like a flying wing type aircraft, and it was down about 150 feet and it just scared the dickens out of them because it was so low.
validated_incidents.occurred_at_text: same night as August 31, 1951 Lubbock photos, about two hours before

validated_incidents.title: Green fireballs over New Mexico
validated_incidents.summary: Multiple reports of greenish-blue fireballs with flat trajectories observed over New Mexico and near Los Alamos, featuring no explosion despite apparent low altitude and size.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: there's a Dr., uh, Lincoln LaPaz down in Albuquerque at the University of New Mexico who's been making a big deal out of these green fireballs. They appear to be, uh, similar to a meteor except that they have a definite flat trajectory. Uh, they're reported to be a brilliant, uh, greenish-blue color, and they, uh, they don't explode.
validated_incidents.occurred_at_text: started in 1949; occur typically in January or December/January period
validated_incidents.location_text: New Mexico, Los Alamos area, Albuquerque
validated_incidents.size_description: about a third or fourth the size of a full moon
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Possibly novel meteor type or aurora-related phenomenon; no fragments recovered; theories include Russian self-destruction missile or new meteor variant

validated_incidents.title: Camp Hood, Texas odd lights outbreak
validated_incidents.summary: An outbreak of odd lights occurred in the Camp Hood, Texas area approximately two years before the 1952 presentation, which were never definitively identified.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: Now, this Camp Hood, Texas concentration was due to an outbreak of odd lights about two years ago. They never did determine exactly what the lights were.
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Special type of report that has not recurred; never determined

validated_incidents.title: New Jersey radar-visual incident with T-33 chase
validated_incidents.summary: T-33 pilots chased a large disc-shaped object near Sandy Hook and Fort Monmouth, New Jersey, followed by multiple radar stations picking up signals tracking at speeds up to 3,500 miles per hour.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: We had a real interesting one from, uh, New Jersey, uh, around Sandy Hook and Fort Monmouth here not too long ago. These pilots in a T-33 chased something, and about 10 minutes later, all our radar stations in that area begin to pick these objects up going back and forth all over the skies.
validated_incidents.location_text: Sandy Hook and Fort Monmouth, New Jersey
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Pilots saw a large balloon launched at Fort Monmouth; radar stations picked up balloons with radar reflectors and possibly ordinary aircraft; operator excitement and procedural error caused false high-speed readings

validated_incidents.title: New Spain Library radar collision course incident
validated_incidents.summary: A GCA radar operator tracked two unidentified objects at 400-500 miles per hour on a collision course with an incoming C-47, and the objects made a turn immediately after the tower broadcast a warning.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: We had one interesting case from New Spay Library and, uh, this GCA operator was, uh, sitting there looking in his scope and all of a sudden he saw these two objects come in. They were coming in about 4 or 500 miles an hour. And at the same time a C-47 was coming in, he was going to land his 47. Well, he noticed they were on a collision course, so he called the tower and said, 'Tell those two unidentified airplanes they're on a collision course with this 47.' So the tower just called in the blind... The tower said there's no other airplanes out there. The radar man said, 'Yes, there is.' The tower just called in the blind and said, 'Uh, you two unidentified airplanes, you're on a collision course with a 47.' And just as they said that, these two returns made a turn.
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Objects responded to tower warning with evasive maneuver; coincidence or intelligent response unclear

validated_incidents.title: B-29 radar bombing run anomalous contact
validated_incidents.summary: During a radar bomb scoring run of a B-29 at St. Louis, radar operators detected an object at 48,000 feet descending at approximately 1,000 miles per hour on a collision course, which then maneuvered and disappeared.
validated_incidents.raw_excerpt: For example, I was talking to some people from SAC the other day, and they were telling me about a radar bomb scoring run of a B-29 out at St. Louis. And they were following the B-29 in to the initial point. The operator noticed this plane flying or an object at 48,000 feet. The B-29 was at 25,000 feet. He immediately thought, 'Well, that's possible.' I mean, double harmonics or something, and anyway, he explained it away in his own mind. Well, then the blip started descending on a collision course, and a quick check revealed that it was descending at a rate of something like 1,000 miles an hour.
validated_incidents.resolution_notes: Possibly atmospheric phenomenon or radar artifact; object made turns and disappeared
